title: Heliotropium amplexicaule

{{Short description|Species of flowering plant in the borage family}} {{speciesbox |image =Heliotropium amplexicaule 1DS-II 6150.jpg |genus = Heliotropium |species = amplexicaule |authority = [[Martin Vahl (botanist)|Vahl]] |synonyms = ''Cochranea anchusifolia''
''Heliotropium anchusifolium'' }} '''''Heliotropium amplexicaule''''' is a species of [[Heliotropium|heliotrope]] known by several common names, including '''clasping heliotrope''', '''blue heliotrope''', and '''summer heliotrope'''. It is native to South America, especially [[Argentina]], but it is known on several other continents where it is an [[introduced species]], and in some areas such as eastern [[Australia]], a [[noxious weed]]. It was first described in 1794 by [[Martin Vahl]].{{APNI2|name=''Heliotropium amplexicaule''|id=88977|access-date=2025-01-04}}Vahl, M.(H.) (1794), [https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/9752/?offset=#page=25 ''Symbolae Botanicae: Heliotriopium amplexicaule''] 3: 21 This is a clumpy perennial herb growing branching, hairy stems to about {{Convert|0.5|m|sp=us}} in maximum height. It has abundant foliage of oblong wavy-edged green leaves four to nine centimeters long. The curving terminal spike [[inflorescence]]s hold several tiny bright purple flowers with rounded lobes and tubular yellow throats. The fruits are paired rough-surfaced nutlets. [[Biological pest control]] is being investigated for reducing the spread of this plant in [[New South Wales]] and surrounding areas in Australia. The blue heliotrope leaf beetle, ''[[Deuterocampta quadrijuga]]'', has shown promise, as has the [[flea beetle]] now called blue heliotrope flea beetle (''[[Longitarsus]]'' spp.). ==Toxicity== ''Heliotropium amplexicaule'' contains [[pyrrolizidine alkaloids]] and is [[poisonous]].The MERCK Veterinary Manual, Table 5. {{cite web |url=http://www.merckvetmanual.com/mvm/htm/bc/ttox05.htm |title=Important Poisonous Vascular Plants of Australia |accessdate=2010-11-17 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101117170853/http://www.merckvetmanual.com/mvm/htm/bc/ttox05.htm |archivedate=2010-11-17 }} This plant competes with desirable pastures and causes toxicity to stock.[http://www.dpi.nsw.gov.au/agriculture/pests-weeds/weeds/profiles/blue-heliotrope Weed profile: Blue heliotrope] Retrieved 19 May 2009 ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=27903 Jepson Manual Treatment] *[http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Heliotropium~amplexicaule New South Wales Flora] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20080615215050/http://www.ento.csiro.au/weeds/blueheliotrope/index.html Biological Control] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20071023024816/http://alabamaplants.com/Bluealt/Heliotropium_amplexicaule_page.html Photo gallery] {{Taxonbar|from=Q13552641}} [[Category:Heliotropium|amplexicaule]] [[Category:Flora of Southern America]] [[Category:Taxa named by Martin Vahl]] [[Category:Plants described in 1794]] {{Boraginales-stub}}
